doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Favorite recordings and preferred studio sound
summary: He names the John Bunch duo record as his best work and wants a Telefunken ribbon mic.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well I was looking at your discography list. You’ve played in lots and lots of sessions. Do you have any personal favorites? I know the John Bunch duo record got some real nice press.

That’s one of my favorites. I mean I’d say that’s my best work to date. It’s hard. I don’t like talking about my own work so much, except from a technical viewpoint. Artistically it’s up to you. But I dig that one. I never was really happy with my sound until fairly recently. It’s an interesting phenomenon.
What do you like to see then when you go into a studio now? If you can tell the engineer exactly what you want, what’s it going to be?
I want a 60 year old Telefunken ribbon mic and that’s it.
I’m not sure a ribbon mic would—

Like those big mics they used to use for like the vocalists, way back then. They have the fattest, warmest sound. There’s a large surface area that vibrates, it’s good for low frequencies, it’s good for the human voice and it’s good for the human voice-like qualities of string instruments.
